title: Diagnose a failed VCF task from its logs and events instead of guessing
prompt:
Implement `VcfFailureTriage/VcfFailureTriage.psm1` as a PowerShell 7.4 module for VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0. An SDDC Manager task has ended FAILED and the operator needs a diagnosis rather than a guess. The module reads that task, pulls the events SDDC Manager raised while it was running, and collects a support bundle scoped to exactly what failed. Nothing about the collection may be assumed: the failing sub-tasks decide which component logs are collected, and the events that name their resources decide which domain and which clusters the collection covers.

The environment installs the genuine `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.SddcManager` PowerCLI module version `13.5.0.25380678` and its dependencies as prerequisites. Import and use its generated bindings for every API call and every request model. Do not install, download, copy, generate, vendor, intercept, redefine, imitate or replace VMware modules, assemblies, specifications, harness tools or their results. Do not bypass the SDK with `Invoke-WebRequest`, `Invoke-RestMethod`, `System.Net.Http`, `WebClient`, curl, wget, raw sockets or a subprocess. The caller owns the supplied connected server; do not connect, disconnect, mutate or dispose it.

Read protected `docs/contract.json` and `docs/official_sources.json` first. That focused contract was derived directly from `specifications/sddc-manager/sddc-manager-openapi.json` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at tag `9.0.0.0`, immutable commit `85151f6b1bb58f13b6ac0304bfec53904bea085f`. A rendered documentation page is not a contract source, and the `9.1.0.0` revision of that same specification file is a different contract. Use exactly the operationIds `getTask`, `getNotifications`, `startSupportBundle` and `getSupportBundleStatus`.

Export exactly one function:

`Invoke-VcfFailureTriage -Server <VcfSddcManagerServer> -TaskId <string> [-IncludeHealthCheck] [-ForceCollection] [-PollIntervalSeconds <0..60>] [-TimeoutSeconds <1..900>]`

Requirements:

- Reject a null server or a blank `TaskId` before any request. Defaults are `PollIntervalSeconds=5` and `TimeoutSeconds=300`. A zero poll interval must be supported.
- Normalize every status by trimming, replacing whitespace with underscores and uppercasing invariantly. Compare identifiers, resource types and resource names ordinal case-sensitively.
- Step one calls `getTask` for `TaskId`. `PENDING` and `IN_PROGRESS` mean the task has not ended, and a terminal status other than `FAILED` is not a failure; both throw `InvalidOperationException`. Walk the sub-task tree depth first in response order and keep every sub-task whose own status is `FAILED`. The affected resources are the resources those sub-tasks carry, first seen first, and not the task's own resource list, which names everything the operation was submitted for. The failure's `errorCode`, `message` and `referenceToken` come from the task's first error.
- Step two calls `getNotifications`, which takes no parameters and returns every event there is. An event is correlated when it names at least one affected resource id and its creation timestamp falls inside the task's window, from the task's creation timestamp to its completion timestamp inclusive; parse timestamps invariantly and round trip, and an event with no readable creation timestamp is not correlated. Require at least one correlated event. Correlated events that carry a domain must all carry the same domain id, and the collection's domain name is that domain's name; more than one domain, or none at all, throws `InvalidOperationException`. The cluster names are the names of the `CLUSTER` resources the correlated events name, first seen first and deduplicated.
- Step three calls `startSupportBundle` with a scope of exactly one `Domains` entry for that domain name, carrying the cluster names only when the correlated events named any. `logs` always asks for `sddcManagerLogs` and `apiLogs`, plus `esxLogs`, `vcLogs` or `nsxLogs` for each affected resource of type `ESXI`, `VCENTER` or `NSXT_MANAGER`. `includeFreeHosts` is asked for only when an affected `ESXI` resource is named by no correlated event. `-ForceCollection` asks for `options.config.force`, `-IncludeHealthCheck` asks for `options.include.healthCheck`, and neither switch means the body carries no `options` member at all. Require a nonblank identifier from the accepted collection.
- Every request body carries only members this contract's schemas define, and only what the diagnosis actually asked for. A member that is not set is absent from the body: not null, not false, not an empty string, not an empty array and not an empty object. Never send a member that a later API version added to these schemas.
- Step four polls `getSupportBundleStatus` for that identifier, because the 202 acceptance is not the outcome of the collection. `PENDING` and `IN_PROGRESS` are nonterminal. `COMPLETED_WITH_SUCCESS` and `COMPLETED_WITH_FAILURE` are terminal; any other status throws `InvalidOperationException`, and expiry of `TimeoutSeconds`, measured from the first poll, throws `TimeoutException`. Poll once before the first wait.
- Return exactly one `PSCustomObject` whose properties are in this order: `status`, `taskId`, `taskStatus`, `failedSubTaskNames`, `affectedResourceIds`, `domainName`, `clusterNames`, `includeFreeHosts`, `correlatedEventCount`, `correlatedEventMessageIds`, `requestedLogs`, `supportBundleId`, `supportBundleStatus`, `bundleName`, `errorCode`, `errorMessage`, `referenceToken`, `steps`.
  - `status` is `SUCCEEDED` only when the collection ended `COMPLETED_WITH_SUCCESS`, otherwise `FAILED`. `taskStatus` and `supportBundleStatus` are the normalized statuses that were observed.
  - `failedSubTaskNames`, `affectedResourceIds` and `clusterNames` follow the orders described above, and `correlatedEventMessageIds` holds each correlated event's message id in response order. `requestedLogs` names the `logs` members that were asked for, in the member order of this contract's `Logs` schema. `includeFreeHosts` is what was actually asked for.
  - `bundleName`, `errorCode`, `errorMessage` and `referenceToken` are empty strings when the documents carry none.
  - `steps` holds four objects in call order, each with the three text properties `operationId`, `status` and `detail`: `getTask` with the normalized task status, `getNotifications` with the correlated event count, `startSupportBundle` with the support bundle identifier, and `getSupportBundleStatus` with the terminal collection status. A step's `status` is `SUCCEEDED` or `FAILED` as that step actually ended.
  - Write no diagnostic output and no partial objects to the success pipeline.
- Run `python3 -B .protected/verify.py`. The protected verifier creates runtime-only tasks, events, identifiers and outcomes; starts six contract-pinned mock instances on ephemeral `127.0.0.1` ports, one whose collection ends `COMPLETED_WITH_FAILURE`, one whose collection ends `COMPLETED_WITH_SUCCESS`, one whose task is still running, one whose collection never leaves `IN_PROGRESS`, and two that must be refused before a single request; drives the function once per instance through a caller-owned genuine SDK connection; and reads each instance's flushed and fsynced JSONL request log. Each mock derives its only callable routes from the four operationIds in `docs/contract.json` and refuses every other operation, as well as any body carrying an unknown member, a member this API version does not define, or a member sent null, empty or false. The verifier asserts the exact ordered methods and targets, the bearer token, the media types, the exact request body, the polled identifier, the reported step outcomes, the diagnosis read from the task and the events, and the omission of every member that was not set. No live VMware endpoint is contacted. Everything under `.protected/` and `docs/`, plus `VcfFailureTriage/VcfFailureTriage.psd1`, is protected. Create only `VcfFailureTriage/VcfFailureTriage.psm1`.
scenario: a cluster expansion task ended FAILED deep inside its sub-task tree, and the support bundle that would explain it can only be scoped from the failing sub-tasks' own resources and the events raised against those resources while the task ran
constraint: the contract-pinned loopback request log proves the exact wire shape of the collection that was requested, the diagnosis it was derived from, and the omission of every member that was not set
